thread:
eli: Customer (acme.example.com - dedicated) hit a wave of SSO failures today. Both GitHub and Google flows return a state_mismatch at our callback, user sees "400 - state_mismatch" after redirect. Repro steps below.

eli: Repro: 1) open login at https://acme.example.com/login 2) click 'Sign in with GitHub' 3) complete on GitHub 4) redirected back to https://acme.example.com/_auth/callback?code=...&state=... -> 400 state_mismatch. Works if we hit the hosted redwood URL directly, fails using their custom domain behind their CDN.

support_bob: Thanks — can you paste the root request & cookie headers from the failing flow? any differences between hosted vs custom domain? :thinking_face:

eli: Pasting sanitized headers from the callback request (failing):

```
GET /_auth/callback?code=abc123&state=ZxY+12%2Babc HTTP/1.1
Host: acme.example.com
Cookie: rw_oauth_state=ZxY+12%2Bdef; rw_session=...; other=...
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 15_6 like Mac OS X)
Referer: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize
X-Forwarded-Proto: https
X-Forwarded-Host: acme.example.com
```

eli: Note the state query is "ZxY+12%2Babc" but cookie has "ZxY+12+def" (plus signs vs percent-encoding).

nina-eng: Interesting. Looks like the CDN or an edge rewrite might be URL-decoding `+` into space when it reconstructs the query, or it's doing an extra round of form-urlencoded normalization. Also, the cookie value looks different — could be the client sending a different cookie (stale) or our state cookie split/truncated by size. Do we have any deploys around the time? @sam-oncall can you check logs for state generation vs lookup?

sam-oncall: I'm pulling the request traces now. Deploybot shows a small config push at 08:12 UTC but not related. Trace for this session (trace id abc-trace-777): state issued = "ZxY%2B12%2Babc" stored server-side; cookie set on start: `Set-Cookie: rw_oauth_state=ZxY%2B12%2Babc; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=None`

sam-oncall: Callback request we got has query state decoded as "ZxY+12 abc" (space in place of %2B) — looks like one of the edge hops is decoding plus into space. That would cause our exact-match check to fail.

support_bob: Does the customer have an edge worker or CDN rule that rewrites querystrings or normalizes encoding? Ask them to check any transform rules or to disable query canonicalization.

eli: They say they have an older fastly config that normalizes query params for cache keys.

nina-eng: Ok that explains it. Two mitigations: 1) We can make our state comparison tolerant to common normalizations (normalize both cookie and incoming state by percent-encoding `+` and spaces to a canonical form before compare). 2) Ask the customer to disable querystring re-normalization for the callback path or pass state in fragment (not recommended). I'd prefer 1) as a short-term fix.

sam-oncall: Agree. I'll open a quick patch to canonicalize state on lookup and add regression tests for `+`, `%2B`, and space cases. @nina-eng can you review? :thumbsup:

nina-eng: On it. Also add logging to surface the raw query vs cookie values for future triage. Keep changes behind a feature flag for rollback if any oddness.

support_bob: I told the customer to temporarily whitelist `/_auth/callback` from query canonicalization in their CDN. They can also test by sending the login flow via the hosted redwood url and setting `next` to their domain (workaround).

eli: Customer confirmed whitelist workaround works immediately. Thanks team.

deploybot: prod:config-rollout succeeded (cfg-2026-08-01) — no runtime changes deployed to auth service.

sam-oncall: Patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth/compare/canonicalize-state-112 (adds normalization + tests). Will schedule canary deploy tomorrow morning.

eli: Closing the escalation after customer verifies whitelist and our upcoming fix. Leaving notes in case similar reports come in. :white_check_mark:
